newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan investment in China rises 37 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan investment in China rises 37 pct in Jan.

text.p: Taiwan's indirect investment in China rose 37 percent in January to US$96.294 million from US$70.471 million in January 1996 despite the government's call to slow investment there, the finance ministry said on Friday.
The ministry's Investment Commission said it approved 27 investment projects in mainland China, down 25 percent from the same month in 1996.
Taiwan investments in China mainly focused in Guangdong, Jiangsu and Shandong provinces, with major investments in electronics and electrical appliance, food and beverage, plastics and textiles.
Taiwan has banned direct investment and trade with China, rival since the end of a Chinese civil war in 1949.

Some 30,000 Taiwan businesses have poured over US$20 billion into the Chinese mainland, making Taiwan one of the leading overseas investors in China -- and China one of Taiwan's most important markets.
Recently Taiwan's government has warned that the island's economy must not become overdependent on the mainland, and several major firms in 1996 called off China projects in apparent compliance.

But business leaders have vowed they would not cut back on investments in China despite concerns about political instability following the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday.
